blocks.title: Half-life
blocks.text: The half-life, t1/2, is the time taken for the concentration of a reactant to fall to half of its original value.

Calculating k by the half-life method means measuring the time for the concentration of a reactant to halve. For a first-order reaction the rate constant and the half-life are related by k = 0.693 / t1/2. A sample of hydrogen peroxide decomposing by a first-order reaction has a half-life of 2 hours: convert to seconds, 2 x 60 x 60 = 7200 s, then k = 0.693 / 7200 = 9.6 x 10^-5 s-1. Sample Problem 7.2: the first-order conversion of cyclopropane to propene has a half-life of 17.0 min; convert to seconds, 17 x 60 = 1020 s, then k = 0.693 / 1020 = 6.79 x 10^-4 dm3 mol-1 s-1.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The unit dm3 mol-1 s-1 belongs to a second-order rate constant. For a first-order reaction k = 0.693 / t1/2 has the unit of 1/time, so k = 6.79 x 10^-4 s-1.
